Macronix: one status register. Amber: a protection bit. Tap a bit to flip it. Clear protection clears BP and SRWD, as -u does, and keeps QE.
Bit names as on most Winbond-type chips. Amber: a protection bit. Tap a bit to flip it (not WEL, BUSY, SUS, LB or R). Clear protection clears BP, SRP and CMP, as -u does, and keeps QE.
%1$s of SR%2$d is clear: tap to set it
%1$s of SR%2$d is set: tap to clear it
Set bit %7$d (%1$s) in status register %2$d of the %3$s (%4$s)? SR%2$d: %5$02X → %6$02X.
Clear bit %7$d (%1$s) in status register %2$d of the %3$s (%4$s)? SR%2$d: %5$02X → %6$02X.

SRP0, SRP1 and SRWD lock the registers (with the WP# pin low, or until the chip is powered off); SRP0 and SRP1 together would lock them for good and are refused. QE, HOLD and WPS change what the pins of the chip do: a board may not boot from it until they are set back.
Another chip is in the programmer: its registers are shown now, tap the bit again.
This chip has no such status register to write.
The last dump, 512 bytes at a time. Address in hex; 00 and FF bytes are dim.
Past the end of the dump (%1$s): the last address is 0x%2$X.

The page of the app on every network of this device, the same as microsnander -W: open http://ADDRESS:PORT in a browser, any user name, this password. Without a password the page is open to anyone who reaches the port. It starts by itself after a reboot and keeps running with the screen off. Plug the programmer in once and choose this app with Always: then nobody has to be at the device.
Off. Settings… to let an operator elsewhere drive the programmer from a browser.
Stopping: an operation of the page ends first…
Cannot listen on port %1$d (taken?): trying again.
An operator is working from the page.

With remote access on, this device joins the camex server and the operator opens the page through it, by the address in the tunnel. It reconnects by itself. Android asks once for the VPN consent; on a device with nobody at it: adb shell appops set org.openipc.microsnander ACTIVATE_VPN allow, then adb shell appops write-settings.
The VPN was not allowed: the tunnel waits for it.
Tunnel: the VPN consent is needed (Allow VPN…, or adb appops)
Turn remote access on first: the tunnel runs with it.
